name: Alibaba Cloud (阿里云) — the cloud business of Alibaba Group Holding Limited
employees: Not disclosed for the cloud business; Alibaba Group headcount 132,165 at 2026-06-30

ownership.ticker: NYSE: BABA / HKEX: 9988 (parent, Alibaba Group Holding Limited)
ownership.notes: A business and legal-entity cluster inside Alibaba Group, not separately listed. PRC operating companies include 阿里云计算有限公司 (Alibaba Cloud Computing Ltd., a variable-interest entity 'involved in the operation of Cloud Intelligence Group') and the wholly owned Hangzhou AliCloud Apsara Information Technology Co., Ltd. Reported as 'Cloud Intelligence Group' through FY2026 (year to 31 Mar 2026) and, from the June 2026 quarter, inside 'AI Cloud and Compute Services' together with the T-Head chip unit. The 2023 full spin-off was cancelled and has not been revived. Alibaba Group has been dual-primary listed in Hong Kong and New York since 28 Aug 2024.

summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Alibaba Cloud is the one Chinese hyperscaler whose data-centre power architecture has a name, a published specification and a disclosed supply contract — Panama, a 10 kV-to-240/336 V DC transformer-rectifier launched with Delta and Zhonhen in 2019 — and its 2026 ESG report says its 'latest generation of data centers is now fully compatible with HVDC power supply architectures up to 800V'. No Alibaba source discloses a solid-state transformer in service; the only SST-adjacent link on the record is a joint innovation centre with Sungrow (2026). It is spending at hyperscale: 'over RMB190 billion' of a RMB380 billion three-year AI and cloud infrastructure plan had been deployed by 30 Jun 2026, management says five-year needs 'will far exceed' that budget, the June-quarter capex alone was RMB67.7B (+75%), and the Apsara Conference (22 Sep 2026) set a target of more than 20 GW of Alibaba Cloud-operated data-centre capacity by 2032 while warning that 'global shortages across the AI data center supply chain' limit its speed. BACKGROUND: Covered as the cloud unit rather than the group, because it is the only part of Alibaba Group that buys data-centre power equipment and it is reported as its own segment. Segment revenue FY2026 (year to 31 Mar 2026) RMB158.1B (+34%), adjusted EBITA RMB14.3B; June 2026 quarter, in the new AI Cloud and Compute Services segment that adds the T-Head chip unit, RMB48.4B (+45%) and adjusted EBITA RMB5.6B (+133%). Omdia puts it first in mainland China cloud infrastructure at 37% (Q4 2025). It operates 107 availability zones in 31 regions. The Pentagon added Alibaba Group to its Chinese Military Companies list on 8 Jun 2026; Alibaba calls the inclusion 'a mistake', and the list does not bar non-Defense buyers or suppliers. Collection gap: Alibaba names no data-centre power supplier in its own filings; every supplier link comes from the supplier's side.
ecosystemRole: We assess Alibaba Cloud as the Chinese hyperscaler that writes its own power architecture and makes suppliers build to it. Basis: Panama was announced jointly by Alibaba's data-centre infrastructure expert, Delta and Zhonhen in November 2019, with Alibaba stating the module efficiency (98.5%) and the equipment saving (40%); Zhonhen's disclosed contracts show Alibaba buying through annual framework tenders signed by Alibaba (China) Co., Ltd. — RMB800 million for Panama in 2021 — and Zhonhen's 2025 report records Panama 2.0, STS and ATS wins at both 'Alibaba self-built rooms and several third-party co-built rooms'. It also designs the rack: the Panjiu AL128 supernode carries up to 350 kW of power per rack through an in-rack busbar, and T-Head's Zhenwu accelerators fill Alibaba's own supernodes. Its role for power sellers is therefore double: the largest single specifier of HVDC in China's cloud market, and a buyer whose 800 V roadmap is stated only as 'compatible', not deployed. Broker estimates, not disclosures, put Zhonhen's share anywhere from about 50% of Alibaba Cloud's HVDC (36Kr) through 80%-plus (Soochow, 2025) to more than 90% of Panama (Shanxi Securities), with Delta at about 20% (Soochow); the '~70%' figure in circulation has no located source.

productsAndServices.name: Alibaba Cloud public cloud — Apsara IaaS/PaaS
productsAndServices.description: 'A comprehensive suite of cloud services based on a three-tiered architecture of infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS), platform-as-a-service (PaaS) and model-as-a-service (MaaS)', built on the Apsara operating system (Shenlong virtualisation, Pangu storage, Luoshen networking). Alibaba says the cloud served about 67% of A-share listed companies in FY2026. It operates 107 availability zones in 31 regions (Sep 2026); regions opened in 2025–2026 include Mexico, Johor, Paris, São Paulo and Zhongwei, and Türkiye, Finland and the Netherlands are promised within 12 months of Apsara 2026.
highlights: Omdia, Q4 2025: mainland China cloud infrastructure US$14.7B (+26%); Alibaba Cloud 37%, Huawei Cloud 17%, Tencent Cloud 10%
Eddie Wu (Aug 2026): 'We operate the largest number of data centers among Asian cloud providers'
Targets set in 2026: US$100 billion of external cloud revenue by calendar 2030 and above 20% profit margin in the AI cloud business
Region counts differ by date and definition: 92 AZs in 29 regions (31 Dec 2025), 34 regions (FY2026 annual report, 31 Mar 2026), 107 AZs in 31 regions (Sep 2026)
productsAndServices.positioning: China's leader on infrastructure revenue, about 20% of cloud revenue overseas (SemiAnalysis); competes with Huawei Cloud, Tencent Cloud and Volcano Engine at home and the US hyperscalers abroad
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct enterprise sales, self-serve and partners; hybrid and financial cloud (IDC: first in China financial cloud six years running)

productsAndServices.name: AI infrastructure — Lingjun clusters, PAI, Panjiu supernodes, HPN networking
productsAndServices.description: Lingjun (灵骏) intelligent computing clusters and the Platform for AI (PAI) are Alibaba's AI-compute services; PAI integrates 'the full suite of the NVIDIA Physical AI software stack' (Apsara 2025). The Panjiu (磐久) AL128 supernode is Alibaba's own rack design: 128–144 GPUs in a custom double-width rack, 'up to 350 kW power supply capacity and 500 kW heat-removal capacity', 2 kW of liquid cooling per GPU, and centralised in-rack busbar power, with compute nodes decoupled from power nodes. Networking is HPN 8.0 (800 Gbps; the Pro version supports over 130,000 ports at 800G in one cluster). Alibaba says it has cut delivery of a large AI data centre to 100 days.
highlights: Panjiu AL128: 350 kW per rack, in-rack busbar, power nodes decoupled from compute nodes (aliyun.com, Oct 2025) — the busbar voltage is not stated
Zhenwu M890 supernode instances in commercial sale; Kimi K3 and Qwen 3.8-Max served on them (Aug 2026)
Management: A100 and V100 GPUs bought in 2018 and 2020 'continue to be used by customers at close to full capacity'
productsAndServices.positioning: An in-house rack and chip stack that makes Alibaba, not a GPU vendor, the author of its rack power envelope
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Cloud instances and dedicated clusters; management says it may also sell T-Head AI servers to data-centre partners and co-build with them
productsAndServices.roadmap: Upgraded supernode with Zhenwu V900 and clusters to 500,000 cards (Apsara 2026); V900 mass production Q1 2027

productsAndServices.name: T-Head (平头哥) chips — Zhenwu accelerators and Yitian CPUs (inside the segment since June 2026)
productsAndServices.description: T-Head designs the Zhenwu PPU accelerators, Yitian CPUs, Panmai SmartNICs and Zhenyue SSD controllers. More than 100,000 Zhenwu PPUs were deployed on Alibaba Cloud's public cloud by March 2026 and more than 500,000 previous-generation chips have shipped. The Zhenwu M890 is 'backed entirely by domestic supply chain'; the Zhenwu V900, announced at Apsara 2026, offers 'three times the performance' of the M890 with 216 GB of memory and 1,200 GB/s of inter-chip bandwidth, and is scheduled for mass production in Q1 2027.
highlights: Management (May 2026): domestic chips 'still show some gap, whether in power consumption or efficiency, versus advanced foreign chips'
Caixin (Jan 2026): Alibaba will support a future T-Head listing; status not re-checked since
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Internal use and external customers (more than 650 for the M890, per the June-quarter call as relayed)

productsAndServices.name: Model-as-a-service — Model Studio (百炼) and the Qwen models
productsAndServices.description: Model Studio sells Qwen and third-party models; its customer base grew eight-fold year on year to March 2026. Qwen models run from Qwen3-Max (Sept 2025) to Qwen3.8-Max (Aug 2026, open weights) with Qwen 4 in training; Qwen has been downloaded more than 3 billion times. From the June 2026 quarter the model labs and the Qwen consumer and office products report in a separate 'AI Labs and Applications' segment; model serving to cloud customers stays in AI Cloud and Compute Services.
highlights: AI-related product revenue RMB12.4B in the June 2026 quarter — the 12th straight quarter of triple-digit growth
Omdia/Frost & Sullivan: first in China enterprise MaaS by revenue (H1 2025); IDC: second to Volcano Engine by token volume

productsAndServices.name: Data-centre power architecture — Panama and HVDC up to 800 V
productsAndServices.description: Panama (巴拿马电源) was launched on 20 Nov 2019 by Alibaba, Delta and Zhonhen: medium-voltage '10KV AC' converted directly to 240 V DC (also 336 V), power-module efficiency 98.5%, 'single-system capacity above 2.5 MW', with Alibaba's data-centre infrastructure expert saying it removes 40% of the equipment; it was then already running at Alibaba data centres in Zhejiang and Jiangsu. Zhonhen describes the product as integrating '10kV distribution, a new-type transformer, an uninterruptible power supply (HVDC) and intelligent distribution units' — a transformer followed by rectifier modules, not a solid-state transformer. Alibaba's 2026 ESG report: 'Our latest generation of data centers is now fully compatible with HVDC power supply architectures up to 800V', after moving from low-voltage AC to HVDC.
highlights: Topology per broker research: a multi-winding phase-shifting transformer feeding rectifier modules with no separate PFC stage (Tianfeng, Nov 2025); Soochow classes Panama with designs that keep the 50 Hz step-down stage, against the SST that removes it
Zhonhen's product matrix now lists Panama at 240/400/800 V; no Alibaba source says an 800 V Panama is deployed
Self-built data-centre PUE 1.187 in FY2026 (1.247 five years earlier); clean electricity 73.6% of self-built data-centre supply; target 100% clean electricity for cloud from 2030
Leased data centres carry PUE-linked clauses in supplier contracts (ESG 2026)
productsAndServices.positioning: The first hyperscaler-specified single-stage medium-voltage-to-DC architecture in China; NVIDIA's August 2026 800 VDC execution paper names the Panama Architecture as a transformer-rectifier implementation of its data-hall DC power block — as an architecture, not as a company
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Specified by Alibaba; bought through framework tenders from Zhonhen and Delta
targetSegments: Alibaba self-built and partner-built data centres

productsAndServices.name: Data-centre build programme — self-built, leased and co-built capacity
productsAndServices.description: Alibaba reports separate PUE series for self-built and leased data centres, so it uses both. Named self-built campuses include Zhangbei (Miaotan), Hangzhou Linping, Heyuan, Shanghai Fengjing, Nantong and Ulanqab. Management said in May 2026 that 'not all of these compute centers will be self-built using our own CapEx ... we will secure some through OpEx leasing arrangements' and co-build with data-centre partners. The HK$80B placing completed on 26 Aug 2026 earmarks about HK$31.9B 'to accelerate the buildout of hyperscale AI data centers' and about HK$47.9B to expand global computing infrastructure.
highlights: Target: more than 20 GW of Alibaba Cloud-operated data-centre capacity by 2032 (Apsara 2026); in 2025 Wu framed it as 10× the 2022 energy scale
Capital commitments contracted but not provided for: RMB54.1B at 31 Mar 2026

No landlord is named by Alibaba; AtHub (数据港) takes 98.30% of its revenue from 'a large internet company' it does not name, and Zhonhen's 2017 filings pair an Alibaba Zhangbei project with AtHub's HB33 — an inference, not a disclosure
SemiAnalysis: GDS and VNET 'captured barely a third of ByteDance and Alibaba orders in 2024–2026YTD'
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Internal capacity; equipment bought by framework tender; leases and co-builds with partners

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that Alibaba Cloud is a specifier-buyer: it designs the power architecture and then buys it from a short supplier list by framework tender. Basis: Panama was announced by Alibaba with Delta and Zhonhen in 2019 with Alibaba stating the specification; Zhonhen's disclosed contracts run from a 2017 Zhangbei HVDC order through a ~RMB300M 2018 HVDC tender to a RMB800M 2021 Panama framework signed by Alibaba (China) Co., Ltd.; Zhonhen's 2025 report shows Panama 2.0, STS and ATS wins in both self-built and partner-built halls. A vendor enters by being written into the architecture, not by bidding against it.

(High confidence) We assess that Panama is a transformer-rectifier and that Alibaba's stated 800 V position is compatibility, not deployment. Basis: Zhonhen and Delta describe a 10 kV transformer feeding rectifier modules; Soochow's taxonomy separates designs that keep the 50 Hz step-down stage (Panama) from the SST that removes it; the 2026 ESG report says its latest data centres are 'fully compatible with HVDC power supply architectures up to 800V' but gives no deployed 800 V capacity. No Alibaba source mentions a solid-state transformer. Indicator to watch: an Alibaba or supplier disclosure of 800 V Panama, or of an SST, in service at an Alibaba campus.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the supplier base is concentrated and now partly battery-owned. Basis: broker estimates range from about 50% of Alibaba Cloud's HVDC to more than 90% of Panama for Zhonhen, with Delta at about 20% (Soochow); CATL signed definitive agreements on 14 Aug 2026 to take 49% of Zhonhen's controlling holdco. Zhonhen's own 2025 report shows its largest single customer at only RMB93.5M, so its Alibaba revenue is either spread across contracting entities and partners or much smaller than in 2021 (RMB319.9M in the first nine months) — no disclosure settles which.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that capacity will increasingly be leased and co-built, which moves part of the equipment decision to landlords working to Alibaba's specification. Basis: Wu (May 2026) — 'not all of these compute centers will be self-built ... we will secure some through OpEx leasing arrangements' and co-build with partners, possibly selling T-Head servers to them; separate PUE series for leased data centres and PUE clauses in their contracts; Zhonhen's wins in 'third-party co-built rooms'. Collection gap: Alibaba names no landlord; AtHub's 98.30% single-customer dependence is consistent with Alibaba but unnamed.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the rack is where Alibaba's power demand is moving fastest. Basis: the Panjiu AL128 supernode already specifies 350 kW per rack on an in-rack busbar with power nodes decoupled from compute; T-Head's Zhenwu V900 supernodes scale to 500,000 cards; management says domestic chips still trail foreign ones on power efficiency. Collection gap: the busbar voltage and the rack power-supply vendors are not disclosed.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the June 2026 1260H listing is a US-facing constraint with limited direct effect on Chinese suppliers. Basis: Alibaba's HKEX statement that the list 'does not impose any other export controls or sanctions, nor does it prohibit any persons (other than the U.S. Department of Defense) from business dealings'; the 20-F nonetheless reports that relationships with business partners 'have been affected' by the prospect of listing. Indicator to watch: any move to the Entity List, which the 20-F names as a risk.

relationships.via: Panama power (巴拿马电源); HVDC; STS and ATS
relationships.note: Zhonhen co-launched Panama with Alibaba and Delta in 2019 and is its principal Panama and HVDC supplier; the 2021 framework contract was RMB799,996,033.57 with Alibaba (China) Co., Ltd.
relationships.context: Zhonhen's disclosures run from 2017 wins at Alibaba's Zhangbei campus, through a ~RMB300M 2018 HVDC and rack-head-cabinet award, to the 2021 Panama framework (about 56% of Zhonhen's 2020 revenue). Its sales to Alibaba and affiliates were RMB88.0M in 2019, RMB298.6M in 2020 and RMB319.9M in the first nine months of 2021. Its 2025 report records Panama 2.0, STS and ATS wins at Alibaba self-built and third-party co-built rooms, but its largest single 2025 customer bought only RMB93.5M. Share estimates are brokers', not Zhonhen's: about 50% of Alibaba Cloud HVDC (36Kr), 80%-plus of 2025 HVDC (Soochow), more than 90% of Panama (Shanxi Securities). No source for the '~70%' figure in circulation was found.

relationships.note: Delta co-launched Panama with Alibaba and Zhonhen on 20 Nov 2019 and supplies Panama and HVDC equipment; Soochow estimates about 20% of Alibaba's 2025 HVDC purchases.
relationships.context: Delta China's launch release quotes Alibaba's data-centre infrastructure expert Liu Shuiwang on 98.5% module efficiency and 40% fewer devices, and says Panama was already running at Alibaba data centres in Zhejiang and Jiangsu. Delta's release credits Delta and Alibaba; independent broker coverage credits all three. Delta reported more than 500 Panama units online across customers by August 2024 (per Tianfeng). The supply share is a broker estimate, not a disclosure.

relationships.note: Sungrow and Alibaba Cloud set up a 'Green Token Joint Innovation Center' in H1 2026 to push AIDC power-supply innovation, unveiled at Sungrow's EnerNeo SST launch.
relationships.context: Sungrow's H1 2026 interim report records the centre; trade coverage describes its scope as green-power direct supply, 800 V DC supply and compute-power coordination. No Alibaba purchase of a Sungrow SST is disclosed.

relationships.note: Narada said on its investor platform that Alibaba Cloud is a customer for which it mainly provides data-centre backup power products.
relationships.context: The statement (relayed February 2025) is Narada's own; neither its 2025 annual report nor its H1 2026 interim names Alibaba. Retail-blog claims about specific tender shares were not used.

relationships.via: A100/V100 installed fleet; Physical AI software stack in PAI
relationships.note: Alibaba runs Nvidia GPUs bought in 2018 and 2020 'at close to full capacity' and integrated Nvidia's Physical AI software stack into PAI in 2025, while replacing externally bought chips with T-Head's where it can.
relationships.context: The 20-F cites US 'export restrictions on advanced computing chips of Nvidia'. China conditionally approved H200 purchases in January 2026; actual Alibaba H200 deliveries are not confirmed in any source located.

relationships.note: ByteDance's Volcano Engine is Alibaba Cloud's closest rival in China's model-API market — first on token volume, while Alibaba leads on revenue — and the other of China's two largest AI-infrastructure spenders.
relationships.context: IDC gave Volcano Engine 49.2% and Alibaba Cloud 27% of China's public-cloud LLM token calls in H1 2025; Omdia and Frost & Sullivan put Alibaba first on enterprise MaaS revenue. SemiAnalysis groups the two as the wholesale market's largest orders.

policyExposure.regime: Section 1260H list (US DoD Chinese Military Companies)
policyExposure.exposure: Alibaba Group was included on 8 Jun 2026 (a February 2026 inclusion had been withdrawn). Under FY2024 NDAA §805 the Defense Department may not contract directly with listed entities from 30 Jun 2026, with a product ban from 30 Jun 2027 (WilmerHale). Alibaba says the list 'does not impose any other export controls or sanctions, nor does it prohibit any persons (other than the U.S. Department of Defense) from business dealings with the Group'.
policyExposure.mitigation: Alibaba calls its inclusion 'a mistake' and says it 'will take all available legal action'.

policyExposure.exposure: The 20-F cites US export restrictions on Nvidia's advanced chips, the House-passed Remote Access Security Act (Jan 2026) that would restrict China-based access to cloud compute on advanced US chips, and a possible new US framework for AI-chip exports; it says access to 'chips and data center services' has been and may be further affected.
